title: Introduce supply-chain KMS attestor and RBAC tamper-guarding hook
author: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Recent compliance reviews highlighted a gap in our supply-chain integrity story: operators and installer tooling could not cryptographically assert that deployable artifacts (helm charts, installer bundles) were provisioned with a customer-scoped KMS key provenance. This limits our ability to produce non-repudiable audit records for Private installations and on-prem flows.

Goals: 1) Add an attestor service that validates a signed provenance blob against configured KMS providers and emits a tamper-evidence header used by RBACv2 decisioning. 2) Integrate a lightweight RBAC hook (tamper-guard) that rejects operator-scoped role grants when provenance checks fail. 3) Provide an operator-facing runbook and CI guards to validate the attestation flow.

What this PR does: Adds a new internal attestor component (pkg/attestor) which consumes artifact metadata, verifies KMS-wrapped signatures across our supported KMS adapters (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault), and returns a signed assertion with a canonicalized audit fingerprint. Introduces an RBAC enforcement hook (pkg/rbac/tamperguard.go) that consults the attestor via gRPC and attaches a tamper-evidence claim into the authorization pipeline. Installer/helm changes wire the attestor sidecar into Private and Dedicated installers with a default disabled flag. Includes e2e CI job and a new compliance runbook that documents expected signals in the audit logs.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-4121) - [x] Unit tests for attestor parsing and KMS adapters - [x] Integration test for attestation + RBAC decision loop - [x] Compliance runbook drafted - [x] Backwards-compatible by default (attestor disabled in hosted API)

Compatibility notes: The tamper-guard is opt-in per-namespace via a new policy flag (rbac.enable_tamper_guard). When disabled, behavior is unchanged. When enabled, operator role grants that lack a valid provenance assertion will receive a scoped denial. Rollout plan: Canary on staging, enable for Private installer images in a gated rollout, then flip default for new installs after 4 weeks of telemetry.

References: Linear ENG-4121, Security ticket SEC-98, SUP-1234 for support escalation.
